title: Orlando Travel Guide

hero.headline: Orlando Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Plan a high-value Orlando itinerary with top neighborhoods, outdoor access, and proven tour ideas.

overview: Orlando is a strong base for culture, food, and outdoor day plans. Build each day around one anchor area, then add nearby experiences to reduce transit time.
For first-time visitors, pair iconic landmarks with one local neighborhood each day. This gives you a more complete feel for Orlando without over-scheduling.

highlights.description: Start with landmark districts and viewpoints during early hours.

highlights.title: Local neighborhoods

highlights.title: Evening experiences

thingsToDo.title: Explore Walt Disney World
thingsToDo.description: Walt Disney World Resort opened on October 1, 1971, in Orange and Osceola counties and covers about 25,000 acres, making it one of the largest entertainment complexes in the world. The property now includes four major theme parks built in phases: Magic Kingdom in 1971, EPCOT in 1982, Disney’s Hollywood Studios in 1989, and Disney’s Animal Kingdom in 1998. Its internal utility and transportation systems were organized through a special district structure historically known as Reedy Creek. Because of that scale and governance model, the resort functions as both an attraction and a regional planning case study, with major effects on employment, road networks, and hotel development across metropolitan Orlando.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Shoulder seasons are best for comfort and flexibility
bullets: Spring and fall typically offer the easiest weather for walking and tours.
Summer can be busy; reserve major attractions and timed entries early.
Winter trips can provide better rates and lighter midday crowds in many districts.

travelTips: Use early starts for major sights and popular viewpoints.
Pre-book top attractions and guided activities during peak months.
Keep one flexible block each day for weather or traffic changes.
Stay close to transit hubs if you want to minimize transfer time.

faq.q: How many days are ideal for Orlando?
faq.a: Three to four days gives enough time for major attractions and one outdoor-focused day.

faq.q: Is Orlando good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. Most itineraries can combine city highlights with nearby hiking, water, or scenic touring options.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For top-rated tours and peak travel weeks, advance booking is strongly recommended.
